question: Can a class-balanced, CV-tuned gradient-boosting cost model with categorical schedule features choose faster compiler schedules on held-out programs than a standard random-forest cost surrogate?
method: Seeded synthetic loop-nest simulator; program-level 70/30 split; each test program's candidate schedules ranked by predicted runtime; mean regret as main metric.

dataset.name: Synthetic loop-nest schedule simulator (seeded numpy generator)

metric_name: mean regret (chosen runtime / best candidate runtime - 1)
baseline: RandomForestRegressor (300 trees, min_samples_leaf=2) on one-hot schedule features plus numeric program features, predicting raw runtime.
improved: LightGBM regressor with native categorical features, hyper-parameters chosen by 3-fold GroupKFold CV on training programs, per-program z-scored log-runtime target and program-balanced sample weights.
notes: Synthetic data, not the paper's dataset; the paper's own method is not reproduced (only a generic random-forest baseline is used). The baseline uses fixed hyper-parameters while the improved model is CV-tuned, so gains may partly reflect tuning. Regret and top-1 use noisy observed runtimes on a modest number of test programs. Seeds vary model randomness only; the data split and generator are fixed at seed 42.
